data.text: The evidence is consistent and clear. Let me confirm the timeline interpretation before reporting.

data.reason: Modem is back OPERATIONAL (registered at 02:28:21, uptime 2280s per modem-metrics), but the WAN interface still holds its pre-outage lease (198.51.100.27) and cannot reach the ISP gateway (100% loss to 198.51.100.1). The watchdog decided a reload was warranted at 02:30 but is in observe mode and only logged 'would_reload'. Reconfiguring the WAN interface renews the DHCP session over the now-working link.

data.cause: The internet dropped when the ISP cable modem lost sync (~02:01, T3 timeout) and re-registered at 02:28, but the firewall's WAN interface kept its pre-outage DHCP session (198.51.100.27 via gateway 198.51.100.1, now unreachable), so traffic still cannot leave the network even though the modem is OPERATIONAL; the WAN watchdog saw this and decided a reload was needed at 02:30 but, in observe mode, only logged "would_reload".
evidence: ping -c 3 -n 198.51.100.1: 100% packet loss to the ISP gateway despite it having an ARP entry (arp -a shows 198.51.100.1 at 00:17:10:9a:a3:96), so L2 is up but the ISP-side path is stale
cat /var/db/dhclient.leases.vtnet0: lease for 198.51.100.27 with router 198.51.100.1, renew not due until 2026/3/5 — the lease predates the outage and was never renewed

tail /var/db/wan-watchdog/modem-events.jsonl: 'No Ranging Response received - T3 time-out' at 02:01:44, 'TFTP failed - configuration file NOT FOUND' at 02:14:10, 'Cable Modem Reboot ... registration complete' at 02:28:21 — a transient provider-line fault that self-healed
cat /var/db/wan-watchdog/modem-metrics.jsonl: modem status NOT_SYNCHRONIZED at 02:06, OPERATIONAL by 02:29 and still OPERATIONAL at 02:40 (uptime 2280s)
tail /var/db/wan-watchdog/events.jsonl: decision 'reload' (modem_operational) at 02:30 and would_reload again at 02:40, mode observe — nothing actually reloaded the WAN
ifconfig vtnet0: WAN UP/RUNNING with LOWER_UP and inet 198.51.100.27 unchanged; netstat -rn still routes default via 198.51.100.1
data.recommendation: Renew the WAN DHCP session on gw.lan (wan_reload) so the interface renegotiates over the now-working cable link — this was requested and its preconditions were met. Afterwards confirm reachability of the ISP gateway and internet; if it recurs, consider letting the watchdog act automatically once the modem reports OPERATIONAL and the settling window passes, and have the ISP check the flaky line (T3 timeouts / missing config file) that triggered the reboot.
data.detail: Stale WAN DHCP session after ISP link blip; lease never renewed
